title: Perform work site fumigation clean-up and clearance and procedures

lessons.title: Aeration and gas clearance testing
lessons.html:
The final danger phase

When a fumigation ends, the structure or commodity still holds a high concentration of toxic gas. Aeration and clearance are the steps that release it safely and confirm that people can return. These steps are done by, or under the direct supervision of, an operator registered for fumigation.

Before aeration

  • Confirm the full exposure period on the label is complete.
  • Check wind direction and speed; plan to vent away from people and buildings.
  • Keep the exclusion zone, signs and guarding in place.
  • Put on the respiratory protection the label specifies, check monitors and brief the standby person.

Aeration steps

  1. Open from outside where possible, starting on the downwind side.
  2. Lift tarps, open vents and doors, or run aeration fans as planned.
  3. Withdraw and wait for the planned venting time while monitoring the perimeter.
  4. Enter only in pairs with protection to open further openings.

Clearance testing

  • Use an instrument or detector tubes suited to the fumigant, checked and in date.
  • Test every room, roof space, cupboard, bin headspace and the commodity.
  • Test soft materials such as mattresses, bags and sacks, which release gas slowly.
  • Compare all readings with the label re-entry level and the occupational exposure requirements.
  • Continue aeration and retest where any reading is too high.

Never judge clearance by smell. Some fumigants have no smell, and smell is never a reliable sign of a safe level.

lessons.title: Residues, equipment and hand-back
lessons.html:
Handling fumigant residues

Spent residues from aluminium or magnesium phosphide products may still contain material that can release phosphine.

  • Collect residues from trays, sachets or blankets wearing the PPE the label requires.
  • Deactivate or dispose of them strictly as the label directs.
  • Never put residues in closed containers, sealed bags, drains or water unless the label procedure says so, because gas build-up can cause fire or explosion.
  • Never leave residues on site where people or animals can reach them.

Equipment and materials

  1. Remove tape, seals and sampling lines.
  2. Inspect tarpaulins and sheets for damage, clean them, fold and store them dry.
  3. Check sand snakes and repair splits.
  4. Check and clean respirators; record canister use and replace as required.
  5. Return gas monitors for charging and calibration as scheduled.
  6. Return any unused fumigant to locked, ventilated storage and update the stock register.

Clearance certificate and hand-back

ItemContent
Clearance certificateSite, structure, fumigant, clearance date and time, readings, name and registration of fumigator
Client briefingResult, any precautions, ventilation advice, follow-up inspection date
SignageRemoved only after clearance is certified

Walk through the site with the client, check for damage, and confirm that interconnected equipment can be released from lockout. Complete the full fumigation record and reconcile the fumigant used.

Key points

  • Aerate only after the full exposure period, from outside and downwind first, with the zone in place.
  • Test every space and soft materials with suitable instruments, never by smell.
  • Clear only when all readings are below the label re-entry level.
  • Handle phosphide residues strictly per the label and never seal them in closed containers.
  • Clean and store equipment, issue the clearance certificate and remove signs only after clearance.
